inputs.abstract:
A formalisation of the semi-invertible multiplicative ergodic theorem for strongly measurable,
forward-integrable cocycles $\mathcal L$ of bounded operators on a separable Banach space $X$,
over an invertible ergodic transformation of a Lebesgue probability space. No invertibility or
injectivity of the operators $\mathcal L_\omega$ is assumed.

The Lyapunov exponents are defined through the growth rates $\chi_k$ of the Bernstein numbers of
the iterates $\mathcal L^{(n)}_\omega$, and the distinct exponents $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots$
are read off from them. The main result is the Oseledets decomposition: for each $l$ the space
splits almost surely as $X = E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega) \oplus V_l(\omega)$
into equivariant, measurable, finite-dimensional fast spaces $E_i(\omega)$, on which the cocycle
grows at rate exactly $\lambda_i$ both in norm and in slowest growth, and an invariant slow space
$V_l(\omega) = \{x : \lambda_\omega(x) \le \lambda_l\}$, with strongly measurable, tempered
projections. The decomposition is nontrivial exactly when the cocycle is quasicompact.

The submission also proves that the decomposition is unique, that the sum of the first $i$ fast
spaces is exactly the set of vectors admitting a backward history decaying at rate $\lambda_i$,
and that the index of compactness $\lim_k \chi_k$ agrees with the growth rate of the distance of
$\mathcal L^{(n)}_\omega$ to the compact operators, so that quasicompactness can be read off from
that growth rate. The proofs include a version of Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem for
balanced time intervals, and Birkhoff's ergodic theorem.

concepts.title: Backward characterisation of the fast spaces
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$, let
$(L, (\lambda_i), (m_i), (E_i), (V_l), (\Pi_l))$ be an Oseledets decomposition of $\mathcal{L}$,
and let $B_c(\omega)$ be the set of vectors with a backward history at $\omega$ decaying at
rate $c$. Then for every $i < L$ and almost every $\omega$,
$$E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_i(\omega) = B_{\lambda_i}(\omega).$$
In finite dimensions, and with an integrability assumption on the inverse, this is close to
Lemma 20 of Froyland, Lloyd and Quas (2013).
With zero-based indices the statement reads
`fastSum E i ω = backwardSet R ω (lam i)` for `i + 2 ≤ Lval`.

concepts.title: Backward histories
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a Banach space $X$ over $(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$. A *backward
history* of $x \in X$ at $\omega$ is a sequence $y_0 = x, y_1, y_2, \ldots$ in $X$ with
$$\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^{-(n+1)}\omega}\, y_{n+1} = y_n \quad \text{for all } n \ge 0,$$
so that $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega}\, y_n = x$. For $c \in [-\infty, \infty]$,
$B_c(\omega)$ is the set of $x \in X$ having a backward history that decays at rate $c$:
$$\limsup_n \tfrac1n \log \|y_n\| \le -c,$$
that is, for every real $b < c$, $\|y_n\| \le e^{-bn}$ for all large $n$. In Lean
$\sigma^{-n}\omega$ is written `σ.symm^[n] ω`.

namespace Lax606786.BackwardHistories

open Filter
open Lax606786.Cocycles

/-- `B_c(ω)`: the vectors with a backward history along `σ^{-n}ω` decaying at rate `c`. -/
def backwardSet {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]
    (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) (c : EReal) : Set X :=
  {x | ∃ y : ℕ → X, y 0 = x ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, R.L ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n + 1] ω) (y (n + 1)) = y n) ∧
    ∀ b : ℝ, (b : EReal) < c → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ‖y n‖ ≤ Real.exp (-b * n)}

end Lax606786.BackwardHistories

concepts.title: Kingman's theorem for balanced intervals
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma$ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a Lebesgue
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ (a standard Borel space with a probability measure giving
points measure zero), and let $(f_n)$ be a subadditive family of integrable functions over
$\sigma$. Then the averages over the balanced time intervals $[-n, n)$ converge to the same
constant as in Kingman's theorem:
$$\tfrac{1}{2n} f_{2n}(\sigma^{-n}\omega) \to C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\mu
  \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,$$
with $C \in [-\infty, \infty)$ and limits taken in the extended reals. This is the balanced
subadditive ergodic theorem of Lee (2024).

/-!
---
title: Kingman's theorem for balanced intervals
type: theorem
---
Let $\sigma$ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a Lebesgue
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ (a standard Borel space with a probability measure giving
points measure zero), and let $(f_n)$ be a subadditive family of integrable functions over
$\sigma$. Then the averages over the balanced time intervals $[-n, n)$ converge to the same
constant as in Kingman's theorem:
$$\tfrac{1}{2n} f_{2n}(\sigma^{-n}\omega) \to C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\mu
  \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,$$
with $C \in [-\infty, \infty)$ and limits taken in the extended reals. This is the balanced
subadditive ergodic theorem of Lee (2024).
-/

namespace Lax606786.BalancedKingman

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology
open Lax606786.SubadditiveFamilies

/-- `f_{2n}(σ^{-n} ω) / 2n` converges almost everywhere to `C = lim (1/n) ∫ f_n`. -/
axiom balancedKingman {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [NullSingletonClass μ]
    (σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω) (hσ : Ergodic σ μ) (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (hf : IsSubadditiveFamily σ f)
    (hint : ∀ n, Integrable (f n) μ) :
    ∃ C : EReal, C ≠ ⊤ ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (((∫ ω, f n ω ∂μ) / n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f (2 * n) ((σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω) / (2 * n) : EReal))
        atTop (𝓝 C)

end Lax606786.BalancedKingman

concepts.title: Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma$ be an ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a probability space
$(\Omega, \mu)$ and let $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable and integrable. Then the
Birkhoff averages converge to the space average almost everywhere:
$$\frac1n \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(\sigma^k \omega) \to \int f \, d\mu
  \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega.$$
The theorem is due to Birkhoff (1931).

concepts.title: Cocycles and their Lyapunov exponents
concepts.description:
A **cocycle** consists of an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation $\sigma$ of a
Lebesgue probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ (a standard Borel space with a probability measure
giving points measure zero), together with a map $\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omega$ from
$\Omega$ into the bounded operators on a real Banach space $X$ which is

- *strongly measurable*: $\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omega x$ is measurable for each $x \in X$;
- *forward integrable*: $\log^+ \|\mathcal{L}_\omega\| \in L^1(\mu)$.

No invertibility of $\mathcal{L}_\omega$ is assumed. Its iterates are
$\mathcal{L}^{(0)}_\omega = \mathrm{id}$ and
$\mathcal{L}^{(n+1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}_{\sigma^n \omega} \circ \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega$.

All logarithms below take values in $[-\infty, \infty)$ with $\log 0 = -\infty$, and indices of
exponents are shifted by one from the usual convention: `lambda 0` is $\lambda_1$.

- The **growth rate of a vector** is
  $\lambda_\omega(x) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega x\|$.
- The **$k$-th Lyapunov exponent** ($k \ge 1$) is
  $\chi_k(\omega) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega)$, with
  $\rho_k$ the Bernstein number. The sequence $\chi_1 \ge \chi_2 \ge \cdots$ is non-increasing and
  $\chi_1 = \lambda_1$ is the top exponent.
- The **distinct exponents** $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots$ are the distinct values of
  $\chi_k$: $\lambda_1 = \chi_1$ and $\lambda_{i+1} = \chi_t$ for the least $t$ with
  $\chi_t < \lambda_i$. The **multiplicity** $m_i$ of $\lambda_i$ is the number of $k$ with
  $\chi_k = \lambda_i$. When there is no exponent after $\lambda_i$ the recursion stops: $m_i$ is
  recorded as $0$, and the later $\lambda$'s are $-\infty$.
- The **index of compactness** is $\nu(\omega) = \lim_k \chi_k(\omega) = \inf_k \chi_k(\omega)$.
- The cocycle is **quasicompact** if $\nu < \lambda_1$ almost everywhere.
- A family of operators $\omega \mapsto P_\omega$ is **tempered** if
  $\omega \mapsto \log \|P_\omega\|$ is tempered for $(\sigma, \mu)$.

  /-- The invariant measure. -/
  μ : Measure Ω
  /-- The generator `ω ↦ 𝓛_ω`. -/
  L : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
  isProbability : IsProbabilityMeasure μ
  nullSingleton : NullSingletonClass μ
  ergodic : Ergodic σ μ
  stronglyMeasurable : ∀ x : X, Measurable (fun ω => L ω x)
  forwardIntegrable : Integrable (fun ω => Real.log (max ‖L ω‖ 1)) μ

attribute [instance] Cocycle.isProbability Cocycle.nullSingleton

namespace Cocycle

/-- `𝓛^{(n)}_ω = 𝓛_{σ^{n-1}ω} ∘ ⋯ ∘ 𝓛_ω`. -/
noncomputable def iterate (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
  | 0, _ => ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X
  | n + 1, ω => (R.L (R.σ^[n] ω)).comp (R.iterate n ω)

/-- `λ_ω(x) = limsup (1/n) log ‖𝓛^{(n)}_ω x‖`. -/
noncomputable def lambdaAt (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) (x : X) : EReal :=
  limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal ‖R.iterate n ω x‖ / (n : EReal)) atTop

/-- `χ_k(ω) = limsup (1/n) log ρ_k(𝓛^{(n)}_ω)`. Meaningful for `k ≥ 1`; `χ_0 = -∞`. -/
noncomputable def chi (R : Cocycle Ω X) (k : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
  limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal (bernsteinNumber (R.iterate n ω) k) / (n : EReal)) atTop

/-- The index `k` at which the `(i+1)`-st distinct exponent first occurs among the `χ_k`:
`1` for `i = 0`, then the least `t ≥ 1` with `χ_t` below the previous distinct exponent,
and `0` once there is none. -/
noncomputable def lambdaIdx (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → ℕ
  | 0, _ => 1
  | (i + 1), ω => sInf {t : ℕ | 1 ≤ t ∧ R.chi t ω < R.chi (R.lambdaIdx i ω) ω}

/-- `lambda i` is the distinct exponent `λ_{i+1}`. -/
noncomputable def lambda (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
  R.chi (R.lambdaIdx i ω) ω

/-- `mult i` is the multiplicity `m_{i+1}` of `λ_{i+1}`; `0` if `λ_{i+1}` is the last distinct
exponent. -/
noncomputable def mult (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : ℕ :=
  R.lambdaIdx (i + 1) ω - R.lambdaIdx i ω

/-- `ν(ω) = inf_{k ≥ 1} χ_k(ω)`. -/
noncomputable def nu (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) : EReal := ⨅ k : ℕ, R.chi (k + 1) ω

/-- `ν < λ₁` almost everywhere. -/
def IsQuasicompact (R : Cocycle Ω X) : Prop :=
  ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.nu ω < R.chi 1 ω

/-- `ω ↦ log ‖P_ω‖` is tempered. -/
abbrev IsTempered (R : Cocycle Ω X) (P : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X) : Prop :=
  Tempered R.σ R.μ (fun ω => Real.log ‖P ω‖)

end Cocycle

end Lax606786.Cocycles

concepts.title: The Grassmannians of a Banach space
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space. The unit sphere of a subspace $V \le X$ is
$\mathbb{S}_V = \{x \in V : \|x\| = 1\}$; it spans $V$, so it determines $V$.

- The Grassmannian $\mathcal{G} X$ is the set of closed subspaces $V \le X$ admitting a bounded
  projection $X \to V$. It carries the distance
  $$d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W) \in [0, \infty],$$
  the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres (infinite exactly when one of $V, W$ is $0$ and
  the other is not).
- For $k \ge 0$, $\mathcal{G}_k X$ is the set of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $X$. For
  $k \ge 1$ the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}_V$ is a nonempty compact set and $\mathcal{G}_k X$
  carries the metric $d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W)$.

Each is equipped with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of its distance.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Analysis.RCLike.Lemmas
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Closeds

/-!
---
title: The Grassmannians of a Banach space
type: definition
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space. The unit sphere of a subspace $V \le X$ is
$\mathbb{S}_V = \{x \in V : \|x\| = 1\}$; it spans $V$, so it determines $V$.

- The Grassmannian $\mathcal{G} X$ is the set of closed subspaces $V \le X$ admitting a bounded
  projection $X \to V$. It carries the distance
  $$d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W) \in [0, \infty],$$
  the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres (infinite exactly when one of $V, W$ is $0$ and
  the other is not).
- For $k \ge 0$, $\mathcal{G}_k X$ is the set of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $X$. For
  $k \ge 1$ the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}_V$ is a nonempty compact set and $\mathcal{G}_k X$
  carries the metric $d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W)$.

Each is equipped with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of its distance.
-/

namespace Lax606786.Grassmannian

open TopologicalSpace

variable (X : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]

/-- `𝒢X`: the closed subspaces of `X` admitting a bounded projection onto them. -/
def Grassmannian : Type _ :=
  {V : Submodule ℝ X // V.ClosedComplemented}

variable {X}

/-- Every subspace is spanned by its unit sphere. -/
theorem span_sphere_inter (V : Submodule ℝ X) :
    Submodule.span ℝ (Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V : Set X)) = V := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact Submodule.span_le.2 Set.inter_subset_right
  · intro x hx
    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
        rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
      rw [hxeq]
      refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
        inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

namespace Grassmannian

/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
def sphere (V : Grassmannian X) : Set X :=
  Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V.1 : Set X)

/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a closed subset of `X`. -/
def toCloseds (V : Grassmannian X) : Closeds X :=
  ⟨V.sphere, Metric.isClosed_sphere.inter V.2.isClosed⟩

theorem toCloseds_injective : Function.Injective (toCloseds (X := X)) := by
  intro V W h
  apply Subtype.ext
  rw [← span_sphere_inter V.1, ← span_sphere_inter W.1]
  exact congrArg (fun s : Closeds X => Submodule.span ℝ (s : Set X)) h

/-- The distance on `𝒢X`: the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. -/
noncomputable instance instEMetricSpace : EMetricSpace (Grassmannian X) :=
  EMetricSpace.induced toCloseds toCloseds_injective inferInstance

/-- The Borel `σ`-algebra of that distance. -/
noncomputable instance instMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (Grassmannian X) :=
  borel (Grassmannian X)

instance instBorelSpace : BorelSpace (Grassmannian X) := ⟨rfl⟩

end Grassmannian

variable (X)

/-- `𝒢_k X`: the `k`-dimensional subspaces of `X`. -/
def GrassmannianFin (k : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  {V : Submodule ℝ X // FiniteDimensional ℝ V ∧ Module.finrank ℝ V = k}

variable {X}

namespace GrassmannianFin

/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
def sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : Set X :=
  Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V.1 : Set X)

/-- `V` is the span of its unit sphere. -/
theorem span_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    Submodule.span ℝ V.sphere = (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact Submodule.span_le.2 Set.inter_subset_right
  · intro x hx
    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
        rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
      rw [hxeq]
      refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
        inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

/-- `𝕊_V` is compact. -/
theorem isCompact_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : IsCompact V.sphere := by
  have : FiniteDimensional ℝ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := V.2.1
  have himg : V.sphere =
      (Subtype.val : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) → X) '' Metric.sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1 := by
    ext x
    simp only [sphere, Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_image]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hx1, hxV⟩
      refine ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩, ?_, rfl⟩
      rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hx1 ⊢
    · rintro ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hv
      exact ⟨by rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm], v.2⟩
  rw [himg]
  exact (_root_.isCompact_sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1).image continuous_subtype_val

/-- `𝕊_V` is nonempty when `k ≠ 0`. -/
theorem nonempty_sphere {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : V.sphere.Nonempty := by
  have hne : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) ≠ ⊥ := by
    intro h
    apply NeZero.ne k
    have hfr := V.2.2
    rw [h, finrank_bot] at hfr
    exact hfr.symm
  obtain ⟨x, hxV, hx0⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hne
  refine ⟨‖x‖⁻¹ • x, ?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hxV⟩
  rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a nonempty compact subset of `X`. -/
noncomputable def toNonemptyCompacts {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    NonemptyCompacts X where
  carrier := V.sphere
  isCompact' := V.isCompact_sphere
  nonempty' := V.nonempty_sphere

theorem toNonemptyCompacts_injective (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    Function.Injective (toNonemptyCompacts (X := X) (k := k)) := by
  intro V W h
  apply Subtype.ext
  rw [← V.span_sphere, ← W.span_sphere]
  exact congrArg (fun s : NonemptyCompacts X => Submodule.span ℝ (s : Set X)) h

/-- The metric on `𝒢_k X`: the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. -/
noncomputable instance instMetricSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : MetricSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
  MetricSpace.induced toNonemptyCompacts (toNonemptyCompacts_injective k) inferInstance

/-- The Borel `σ`-algebra of that metric. -/
noncomputable instance instMeasurableSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    MeasurableSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
  borel (GrassmannianFin X k)

instance instBorelSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : BorelSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) := ⟨rfl⟩

end GrassmannianFin

end Lax606786.Grassmannian

concepts.title: The index of compactness is the growth rate of the compactness seminorm
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$. If the growth rate of the
compactness seminorm of the iterates exists and is almost everywhere equal to a constant
$\kappa \in [-\infty, \infty]$,
$$\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c = \kappa \quad \text{for a.e. } \omega,$$
then the index of compactness $\nu = \lim_k \chi_k$ equals $\kappa$ almost everywhere. This is
the equivalence of growth statistics in the appendix of Lee (2024).

concepts.title: Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma$ be an ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a probability space
$(\Omega, \mu)$, and let $(f_n)$ be a subadditive family of integrable functions over $\sigma$.
Then there is a constant $C \in [-\infty, \infty)$ such that
$$C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\mu \qquad \text{and} \qquad
  \tfrac1n f_n(\omega) \to C \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega.$$
Limits are taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$. The theorem is due to Kingman
(1968).

type: theorem
---
Let $\sigma$ be an ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a probability space
$(\Omega, \mu)$, and let $(f_n)$ be a subadditive family of integrable functions over $\sigma$.
Then there is a constant $C \in [-\infty, \infty)$ such that
$$C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\mu \qquad \text{and} \qquad
  \tfrac1n f_n(\omega) \to C \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega.$$

/-- Kingman's theorem: `f_n / n` converges almost everywhere to the constant

axiom kingman {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (σ : Ω → Ω) (hσ : Ergodic σ μ) (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (hf : IsSubadditiveFamily σ f)
    (hint : ∀ n, Integrable (f n) μ) :
    ∃ C : EReal, C ≠ ⊤ ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (((∫ ω, f n ω ∂μ) / n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n ω / n : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C)

concepts.title: Growth, Bernstein numbers and the compactness seminorm of an operator
concepts.description:
Let $T : X \to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between real normed spaces.

- The **growth** of $T$ on a subspace $V \subseteq X$ is the slowest growth of a unit vector of
  $V$,
  $$g(T, V) = \inf_{x \in \mathbb{S}_V} \|Tx\|,$$
  with the convention $\inf \emptyset = 0$ (so $g(T, \{0\}) = 0$).
- For $T : X \to X$ and $k \ge 0$, the **$k$-th Bernstein number** is
  $$\rho_k(T) = \sup_{V \in \mathcal{G}_k X} g(T, V).$$
  In particular $\rho_1(T) = \|T\|$, and $\rho_k(T) = 0$ when $k > \dim X$.
- The **compactness seminorm** of $T : X \to X$ is its distance to the compact operators,
  $$\|T\|_c = \inf \{\|T - K\| : K \text{ compact}\}.$$
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.Grassmannian
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.Basic

/-!
---
title: Growth, Bernstein numbers and the compactness seminorm of an operator
type: definition
---
Let $T : X \to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between real normed spaces.

- The **growth** of $T$ on a subspace $V \subseteq X$ is the slowest growth of a unit vector of
  $V$,
  $$g(T, V) = \inf_{x \in \mathbb{S}_V} \|Tx\|,$$
  with the convention $\inf \emptyset = 0$ (so $g(T, \{0\}) = 0$).
- For $T : X \to X$ and $k \ge 0$, the **$k$-th Bernstein number** is
  $$\rho_k(T) = \sup_{V \in \mathcal{G}_k X} g(T, V).$$
  In particular $\rho_1(T) = \|T\|$, and $\rho_k(T) = 0$ when $k > \dim X$.
- The **compactness seminorm** of $T : X \to X$ is its distance to the compact operators,
  $$\|T\|_c = \inf \{\|T - K\| : K \text{ compact}\}.$$
-/

namespace Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

open Lax606786.Grassmannian

variable {X Y : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace ℝ Y]

/-- `g(T, V) = inf {‖T x‖ : x ∈ V, ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
noncomputable def growth (T : X →L[ℝ] Y) (V : Submodule ℝ X) : ℝ :=
  sInf ((fun x : X => ‖T x‖) '' (Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V : Set X)))

/-- `ρ_k(T) = sup {g(T, V) : V ∈ 𝒢_k X}`. -/
noncomputable def bernsteinNumber (T : X →L[ℝ] X) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (Set.range fun V : GrassmannianFin X k => growth T (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X))

/-- `‖T‖_c = inf {‖T - K‖ : K compact}`. -/
noncomputable def compactSeminorm (T : X →L[ℝ] X) : ℝ :=
  sInf ((fun K : X →L[ℝ] X => ‖T - K‖) '' {K | IsCompactOperator K})

end Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

concepts.title: The semi-invertible Oseledets decomposition
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$, over an invertible ergodic
base $(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$. Let $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots$ be its distinct Lyapunov
exponents, $m_i$ their multiplicities, and $L \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \infty\}$ the number of
distinct exponents. Then $\lambda_i$ and $m_i$ are almost everywhere constant, $L \ge 2$ if
and only if $\mathcal{L}$ is quasicompact, and there are

- measurable families of subspaces $E_i(\omega)$ of dimension $m_i$ (the *fast spaces*), for
  $i < L$,
- strongly measurable, tempered families of projections $\Pi_{l}(\omega)$, for $2 \le l \le L$,
  with ranges $V_l(\omega)$ (the *slow spaces*),

such that for almost every $\omega$:

1. $\mathcal{L}_\omega E_i(\omega) = E_i(\sigma\omega)$, and $E_i(\omega)$ grows at rate exactly
   $\lambda_i$, both in norm and in slowest growth:
   $$\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega|_{E_i(\omega)}\| =
     \lim_n \tfrac1n \log g(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega, E_i(\omega)) = \lambda_i;$$
2. $X = E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega) \oplus V_l(\omega)$, and $\Pi_l(\omega)$
   is the projection onto $V_l(\omega)$ along $E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega)$;
3. $\mathcal{L}_\omega V_l(\omega) \subseteq V_l(\sigma\omega)$;
4. $V_l(\omega) = \{x \in X : \lambda_\omega(x) \le \lambda_l\}$.

This is the semi-invertible form of Oseledets' multiplicative ergodic theorem (Oseledets 1968;
Froyland, Lloyd and Quas 2013; González-Tokman and Quas 2014), for strongly measurable cocycles on
separable Banach spaces as in Lee (2024).
In other words, $\mathcal{L}$ has an Oseledets decomposition in the sense of the definition
of Oseledets decompositions, whose zero-based indexing the Lean statement follows.

import Lax606786.OseledetsDecompositions

/-!
---
title: The semi-invertible Oseledets decomposition
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$, over an invertible ergodic
base $(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$. Let $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots$ be its distinct Lyapunov
exponents, $m_i$ their multiplicities, and $L \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \infty\}$ the number of
distinct exponents. Then $\lambda_i$ and $m_i$ are almost everywhere constant, $L \ge 2$ if
and only if $\mathcal{L}$ is quasicompact, and there are

- measurable families of subspaces $E_i(\omega)$ of dimension $m_i$ (the *fast spaces*), for
  $i < L$,
- strongly measurable, tempered families of projections $\Pi_{l}(\omega)$, for $2 \le l \le L$,
  with ranges $V_l(\omega)$ (the *slow spaces*),

such that for almost every $\omega$:

1. $\mathcal{L}_\omega E_i(\omega) = E_i(\sigma\omega)$, and $E_i(\omega)$ grows at rate exactly
   $\lambda_i$, both in norm and in slowest growth:
   $$\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega|_{E_i(\omega)}\| =
     \lim_n \tfrac1n \log g(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega, E_i(\omega)) = \lambda_i;$$
2. $X = E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega) \oplus V_l(\omega)$, and $\Pi_l(\omega)$
   is the projection onto $V_l(\omega)$ along $E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega)$;
3. $\mathcal{L}_\omega V_l(\omega) \subseteq V_l(\sigma\omega)$;
4. $V_l(\omega) = \{x \in X : \lambda_\omega(x) \le \lambda_l\}$.

This is the semi-invertible form of Oseledets' multiplicative ergodic theorem (Oseledets 1968;
Froyland, Lloyd and Quas 2013; González-Tokman and Quas 2014), for strongly measurable cocycles on
separable Banach spaces as in Lee (2024).
In other words, $\mathcal{L}$ has an Oseledets decomposition in the sense of the definition
of Oseledets decompositions, whose zero-based indexing the Lean statement follows.
Measurability of $E_i$ is with respect to the Borel structure of the Grassmannian; strong
measurability of $\Pi_l$ means that $\omega \mapsto \Pi_l(\omega) x$ is measurable for each $x$.
-/

/-- The sum `E_1(ω) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ E_{l+1}(ω)` of the first `l + 1` fast spaces. The fast spaces are only
given at the indices `i` with `i + 2 ≤ Lval`, and the supremum ranges over those. -/
def fastSum {Ω X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] {Lval : ℕ∞} {mdim : ℕ → ℕ}
    (E : ∀ i : ℕ, ((i + 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ Lval → Ω → GrassmannianFin X (mdim i + 1))
    (l : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : Submodule ℝ X :=
  ⨆ (i : ℕ) (hi : ((i + 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ Lval) (_ : i ∈ Finset.range (l + 1)),
    ((E i hi ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)

/-- The data `(Lval, lam, mdim, E, V, P)` is an Oseledets decomposition of `R`: it satisfies
every clause of the semi-invertible Oseledets decomposition theorem. -/
def IsOseledetsDecomposition {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X] (R : Cocycle Ω X)
    (Lval : ℕ∞) (lam : ℕ → EReal) (mdim : ℕ → ℕ)
    (E : ∀ i : ℕ, ((i + 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ Lval → Ω → GrassmannianFin X (mdim i + 1))
    (V : ℕ → Ω → Submodule ℝ X) (P : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X) : Prop :=
  1 ≤ Lval ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, (i : ℕ∞) < Lval → ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.lambda i ω = lam i) ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, ((i + 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ Lval ↔ ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.mult i ω ≠ 0) ∧
  ((2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Lval ↔ R.IsQuasicompact) ∧
  -- measurability and temperedness
  (∀ i hi, Measurable (E i hi)) ∧
  (∀ i, ∀ x : X, Measurable fun ω => P i ω x) ∧
  (∀ i, R.IsTempered (P i)) ∧
  -- the fast spaces
  (∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : ((i + 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ Lval), ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ),
    R.mult i ω = mdim i + 1 ∧
    Submodule.map (R.L ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) ((E i hi ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)
      = ((E i hi (R.σ ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal
        ‖(R.iterate n ω).comp (((E i hi ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)).subtypeL‖ / (n : EReal))
      atTop (nhds (lam i)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal
        (growth (R.iterate n ω) ((E i hi ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)) / (n : EReal))
      atTop (nhds (lam i))) ∧
  -- the decompositions
  (∀ l : ℕ, ((l + 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ Lval → ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ),
    IsCompl (fastSum E l ω) (V (l + 1) ω) ∧
    Submodule.map (R.L ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) (V (l + 1) ω) ≤ V (l + 1) (R.σ ω) ∧
    (P (l + 1) ω).comp (P (l + 1) ω) = P (l + 1) ω ∧
    V (l + 1) ω = LinearMap.range ((P (l + 1) ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ fastSum E l ω, P (l + 1) ω x = 0) ∧
    (V (l + 1) ω : Set X) = {x : X | R.lambdaAt ω x ≤ lam (l + 1)})

end Lax606786.OseledetsDecompositions

concepts.title: Uniqueness of the Oseledets decomposition
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$.
Any two Oseledets decompositions $(L, \lambda, m, E, V, \Pi)$ and
$(L', \lambda', m', E', V', \Pi')$ of $\mathcal{L}$ agree. They have $L = L'$,
$\lambda_i = \lambda'_i$ for $i \le L$, and $m_i = m'_i$ for $i < L$. For every $i < L$ and
almost every $\omega$,
$$E_i(\omega) = E'_i(\omega), \qquad V_{i+1}(\omega) = V'_{i+1}(\omega), \qquad
  \Pi_{i+1}(\omega) = \Pi'_{i+1}(\omega).$$
Nothing is asserted beyond these indices, where the decomposition theorem constrains nothing.

Indices in the Lean statement are zero-based, as in the definition of Oseledets decompositions.

concepts.title: Slow spaces on a separable Banach space need not be measurable
concepts.description:
Let $\Omega = \{\pm1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ with its product $\sigma$-algebra, and let
$X = \ell^1(\mathbb{Z})$. For $\omega \in \Omega$ let
$$\varphi_\omega(x) = \sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \omega_i x_i, \qquad
  V_\omega = \ker \varphi_\omega = \{x \in X : \varphi_\omega(x) = 0\}.$$
Then $X$ is separable and every $V_\omega$ belongs to the Grassmannian $\mathcal{G} X$, but there
is no measurable map $W : \Omega \to \mathcal{G} X$ with $W(\omega) = V_\omega$ for every
$\omega \in \Omega$.

Over the shift $\sigma(\omega)_n = \omega_{n+1}$ with the Bernoulli measure, the operators
$\mathcal{L}_\omega x = \varphi_\omega(x)\, e_0$ form a cocycle of rank one with
$\lambda_1 = 0$, fast space $E_1(\omega) = \operatorname{span}\{e_0\}$ and slow space
$V_\omega$; so separability of $X$ alone does not make the slow spaces measurable. This
example is due to J. A. Horan (PhD thesis, University of Victoria, 2020). The
argument: distinct $V_\omega$ are at distance at least $1$ in $\mathcal{G} X$ and
$V_\omega = V_{-\omega}$, so a measurable $W$ would make every set $S = -S$ measurable, while
there are more such sets than measurable ones.

In Lean a sign $\omega_i \in \{\pm1\}$ is coded by a boolean, `true` for $+1$.

namespace Lax606786.SlowSpaceNonmeasurability

open TopologicalSpace
open Lax606786.Grassmannian

/-- `ω_i ∈ {±1}`, coded by `true ↦ 1` and `false ↦ -1`. -/
def sign (ω : ℤ → Bool) (i : ℤ) : ℝ := if ω i then 1 else -1

/-- `V_ω = {x ∈ ℓ¹(ℤ) : Σᵢ ωᵢ xᵢ = 0}`. -/
def slowSpace (ω : ℤ → Bool) : Set (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℝ) 1) :=
  {x | ∑' i, sign ω i * x i = 0}

/-- `ℓ¹(ℤ)` is separable and each `V_ω` lies in `𝒢X`, but no measurable map `Ω → 𝒢X` takes the
value `V_ω` at every `ω`. -/
axiom slowSpace_not_measurable :
    SeparableSpace (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℝ) 1) ∧
    (∃ W : (ℤ → Bool) → Grassmannian (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℝ) 1),
      ∀ ω, ((W ω).1 : Set (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℝ) 1)) = slowSpace ω) ∧
    ¬ ∃ W : (ℤ → Bool) → Grassmannian (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℝ) 1),
      Measurable W ∧ ∀ ω, ((W ω).1 : Set (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℝ) 1)) = slowSpace ω

end Lax606786.SlowSpaceNonmeasurability

concepts.title: Subadditive families of measurable functions
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma : \Omega \to \Omega$ be a map on a measurable space. A sequence
$(f_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of measurable functions $\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is a **subadditive family**
over $\sigma$ if
$$f_{m+n}(\omega) \le f_m(\sigma^n \omega) + f_n(\omega) \quad \text{for all } m, n \ge 0
  \text{ and } \omega \in \Omega.$$
The typical example is $f_n(\omega) = \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|$ for a cocycle
$\mathcal{L}$ of bounded operators.

import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Real

/-!
---
title: Subadditive families of measurable functions
type: definition
---
Let $\sigma : \Omega \to \Omega$ be a map on a measurable space. A sequence
$(f_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of measurable functions $\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is a **subadditive family**
over $\sigma$ if
$$f_{m+n}(\omega) \le f_m(\sigma^n \omega) + f_n(\omega) \quad \text{for all } m, n \ge 0
  \text{ and } \omega \in \Omega.$$
The typical example is $f_n(\omega) = \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|$ for a cocycle
$\mathcal{L}$ of bounded operators.
-/

namespace Lax606786.SubadditiveFamilies

/-- `(f_n)` is a subadditive family of measurable functions over `σ`. -/
def IsSubadditiveFamily {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (σ : Ω → Ω) (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n, Measurable (f n)) ∧ ∀ m n ω, f (m + n) ω ≤ f m (σ^[n] ω) + f n ω

end Lax606786.SubadditiveFamilies

concepts.title: Tempered functions
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma : \Omega \to \Omega$ be a measurable map and $\mu$ a measure on $\Omega$. A function
$f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is **tempered** if it grows subexponentially along almost every
forward orbit:
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{f(\sigma^n \omega)}{n} = 0 \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega.$$

import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.MeasureSpaceDef

/-!
---
title: Tempered functions
type: definition
---
Let $\sigma : \Omega \to \Omega$ be a measurable map and $\mu$ a measure on $\Omega$. A function
$f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is **tempered** if it grows subexponentially along almost every
forward orbit:
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{f(\sigma^n \omega)}{n} = 0 \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega.$$
-/

namespace Lax606786.TemperedFunctions

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology

/-- `f(σⁿω)/n → 0` for `μ`-a.e. `ω`. -/
def Tempered {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (σ : Ω → Ω) (μ : Measure Ω) (f : Ω → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => f (σ^[n] ω) / n) atTop (𝓝 0)

end Lax606786.TemperedFunctions

proofs.description:
Each `χ_k` is bounded below by the compactness growth rate, and conversely a cover of the image
of the unit ball of controlled cardinality bounds `χ_k` from above for large `k`, as in the
appendix of Lee (2024). The comparison of Bernstein and Gelfand numbers is in the spirit of
Pietsch's theory of `s`-numbers (Pietsch 1974).

The argument of Lee (2024): the balanced intervals `[-n, n)` are covered, up to a set of small
density, by disjoint orbit windows centred at points where the forward averages are already close
to the limit; this covering comes from a form of Rudolph's backward Vitali lemma for invertible
ergodic systems (Rudolph 1990).

Garsia's maximal ergodic theorem (Garsia 1965; see also Rudolph 1990) gives a weak-type maximal
inequality, which extends almost
everywhere convergence from the dense set of coboundaries plus invariant functions (von Neumann's
splitting, von Neumann 1932) to all of `L¹`; ergodicity identifies the limit with the space
average.

Vectors of the fast spaces have backward histories decaying at the required rate; conversely,
the slow component of a vector with such a history also has one, and vanishes. The backward
growth bound on the fast spaces is a density argument in the manner of Mañé's lemma on tempered
functions (Mañé 1983; González-Tokman and Quas 2015, Lemma 15). Froyland, Lloyd and Quas (2013,
Lemma 20) obtain the corresponding bound in finite dimensions by assuming integrability of the
inverse on the fast spaces, which is not needed here.

The exponents and multiplicities are pinned by the Lyapunov spectrum; the fast spaces are
characterised by their growth, and the slow projections by their range and kernel.
Immediate from the identification of the index of compactness.

Steele's proof (Steele 1989) of Kingman's theorem (Kingman 1968): the families are truncated from below, Birkhoff's theorem bounds the upper limit
of the averages, and a covering of the orbit by blocks on which the averages are nearly minimal
bounds the lower limit.

The construction of Lee (2024): the decomposition is built level by level, each fast space being
the top fast space of the cocycle restricted to the previous slow space, with the slow projections
constructed alongside.

Following Rudolph (1990): a backward Vitali covering by long orbit windows, off the null set of periodic points, is cut
into blocks of height `n`; the bottoms of the blocks form the base of the tower.

Horan's example (Horan 2020). Distinct kernels `V_ω` are at distance at least `1` in `𝒢X`, and
`V_ω = V_{ω'}` only for `ω' = ±ω`, so a measurable `W` would make every set `S = -S` measurable. The product
`σ`-algebra is generated by countably many cylinders and so has at most `𝔠` members, while the
symmetric sets number `2^𝔠`.
